# coreex-graphql: Workflow

Full workflow for adding or extending `CoreEx.Data.GraphQL` (GraphQL-lite) on a CoreEx `*.Api` host.

---

## Phase 1 — Clarify Before Writing

| Question | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Target host | — | `*.Api` project. GraphQL-lite is a REST-adjacent query surface; do not offer it for Subscribe/Relay hosts. |
| Already enabled on this host? | Check first | Grep the host's `Program.cs` for `AddCoreExGraphQLLite` and its `AGENTS.md` for a `**GraphQL:**` line. If both absent, this is first-time enablement (Steps 1–2). If present, skip to Step 2 (adding a root) or Step 3 (bulk ref-data). |
| Entities to expose | Ask | Each entity needs an existing `QueryArgsConfig` + `QueryAsync`/`GetAsync` on its read service — GraphQL-lite adds no new query capability of its own. If one is missing, hand off to `coreex-repository` or `coreex-refdata` first. |
| Bulk-expose reference data? | Yes | `AddReferenceDataQueries` exposes every type known to `ReferenceDataOrchestrator` in one call. |
| Enable introspection? | No | Secure-by-default; only opt in for known-safe internal/dev environments. |
| Require authorization on `/query`? | Match host | `MapCoreExGraphQLLite` is anonymous by default — if the host's REST controllers are `[Authorize]`-protected, ask whether `/query` should be too, since it can reach the same data. |

---

## Step 1 — First-Time Enablement (`Program.cs`)

Add the registration and mapping calls. Register scoped-dependency roots via `CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<T>()` inside each resolver — never capture a scoped instance from the root `IServiceProvider` at registration time, since `IGraphQLEngine` is a singleton.

```csharp
// Program.cs — in the services configuration block, alongside AddMvcWebApi()/AddHttpWebApi()
builder.Services.AddCoreExGraphQLLite((o, sp) =>
{
    o.AddQuery<ProductLite>("products", ProductQueryArgsConfig.Default,
            async (qa, pa, ct) => await CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<IProductReadService>().QueryAsync(qa, pa, ct).ConfigureAwait(false))
     // GetIdentifier<TId> reads/converts the named argument (default "id") and throws an ArgumentException, mapped by the engine to ARGUMENT_ERROR, if missing/empty/wrong-typed.
     .AddGet<Product>("product", (args, ct) => CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<IProductReadService>().GetAsync(args.GetIdentifier<string>(), ct));
});

// ... after app.MapControllers():
app.MapCoreExGraphQLLite("/query"); // Pass configure: rb => rb.RequireAuthorization() if the host's REST endpoints are secured.

// Alongside the host's other OpenTelemetry tracing extensions:
builder.WithCoreExTelemetry().WithCoreExGraphQLTelemetry().UseOtlpExporter();
```

**Rules:**
- `MapCoreExGraphQLLite` must be registered **after** `app.MapControllers()`.
- `MapCoreExGraphQLLite` executes through `WebApi.PostAsync<GraphQLLiteResponse>(...)` — the same response pipeline every CoreEx REST endpoint uses, so unexpected exceptions still surface as a standard `ProblemDetails` response rather than an unhandled 500.
- `GraphQLLiteOptions.EnableIntrospection` defaults to `false`. Only set `true` when the user explicitly wants schema introspection (Postman/Nitro/Apollo Sandbox tooling).
- `MapCoreExGraphQLLite` is anonymous by default. Pass `configure: rb => rb.RequireAuthorization()` explicitly to match a secured host.

---

## Step 2 — Add a Root for an Entity

One `AddQuery<T>`/`AddGet<T>` pair per entity, bridging to its **existing** `QueryArgsConfig` and read-service methods — do not invent new filter/sort logic for GraphQL.

```csharp
o.AddQuery<{Entity}Lite>("{entities}", {Entity}QueryArgsConfig.Default,
        async (qa, pa, ct) => await CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<I{Entity}ReadService>().QueryAsync(qa, pa, ct).ConfigureAwait(false))
 // GetIdentifier<TId> reads/converts the named argument (default "id") and throws an ArgumentException, mapped by the engine to ARGUMENT_ERROR, if missing/empty/wrong-typed.
 .AddGet<{Entity}>("{entity}", (args, ct) => CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<I{Entity}ReadService>().GetAsync(args.GetIdentifier<string>(), ct));
```

**When triggered from `coreex-api`:** after that skill adds a REST GET/Query endpoint pair, and the host already has GraphQL enabled, offer to add the matching root here in the same session rather than requiring a separate invocation.

---

## Step 3 — Bulk-Expose Reference Data (Optional)

```csharp
builder.Services.AddCoreExGraphQLLite((o, sp) =>
{
    // Bulk-register every ref-data type known to ReferenceDataOrchestrator as a query root.
    // Prefix defaults to "ref_"; pass null for no prefix. excludeTypes opts specific types out.
    o.AddReferenceDataQueries(sp, ReferenceDataQueryArgsConfig.Default, prefix: "ref_");

    // Mix with regular entity roots as needed.
    o.AddQuery<ProductLite>("products", ProductQueryArgsConfig.Default, async (qa, pa, ct) => ...);
});
```

Every reference data type known to the `ReferenceDataOrchestrator` is exposed — not just types that declare an `AlternateNames` entry. Each root is named `<prefix><name>` (hyphens replaced with underscores), where `<name>` is the type's registered alternate name where one exists, otherwise its own `Type.Name`.

---

## Step 4 — Record Enablement in the Host's `AGENTS.md`

Add (or update) a plain fact line under that host's `## This Host's Feature Configuration` section — no `dotnet new` template symbol is involved; this is a per-host hand-authored fact added as a side effect of running this skill, not a scaffold-time choice:

```markdown
- **GraphQL:** Enabled -- `/query` endpoint via `CoreEx.Data.GraphQL`; roots: `products`, `product`, `ref_*` (reference data)
```

If the section doesn't yet track this fact (older scaffold), add the line directly beneath the existing bullet list in that section — do not invent a new heading.

---

## Guardrails

- **Opt-in only** — never wire GraphQL into a host unless explicitly asked, even if the user is mid-conversation about queries generally.
- **Bridge, never duplicate** — GraphQL-lite roots must reuse the entity's existing `QueryArgsConfig` and read-service methods; do not hand-author separate filter/sort logic for GraphQL.
- **Singleton engine, scoped resolvers** — always resolve scoped dependencies (repositories, application services) per-invocation via `CoreEx.ExecutionContext.GetRequiredService<T>()`; never capture one from the root `IServiceProvider` at registration time.
- **Map after `MapControllers()`** — `app.MapCoreExGraphQLLite(...)` must come after `app.MapControllers()` in the middleware pipeline.
- **Secure-by-default** — `EnableIntrospection` stays `false` and the endpoint stays anonymous unless the user explicitly asks otherwise; flag the mismatch if the host's REST endpoints are `[Authorize]`-protected but `/query` isn't.
- **No mutations/subscriptions** — GraphQL-lite is read-only, single-root-per-selection, forward-pagination-only (`first`/`after`) by design; do not attempt to add mutation support.
- **Record it** — always add/update the `**GraphQL:**` line in the host's `AGENTS.md` once wiring is complete, so a future session doesn't re-ask.
